title: Maximum Subarray Sum With Length Divisible by K
statement: Consider every non-empty contiguous subarray of the integer array `nums` whose length is a multiple of `k`. Return the largest sum that any of these subarrays has. Because `k <= nums.length`, at least one such subarray always exists.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every start and end works in O(n²). Prefix sums do better: with `prefix(i)` the total of the first `i` elements, the subarray between positions `j` and `i` sums to `prefix(i) - prefix(j)` and has length `i - j`. That length is a multiple of `k` exactly when `i` and `j` leave the same remainder modulo `k`. So, for each end position `i`, the best start is the smallest earlier prefix in the same remainder class, and one running minimum per class is all we need.

## Approach

1. `minPrefix[r]` holds the smallest prefix sum seen at a position with remainder `r`. Position 0 (no elements, sum 0) belongs to class 0; the other classes start empty (`Infinity`).
2. For `i` from 1 to `n`, add `nums[i - 1]` to `prefix`.
3. With `slot = i % k`, the best subarray ending here sums to `prefix - minPrefix[slot]`; keep the larger of that and `best`.
4. Only then record `prefix` in `minPrefix[slot]` for later positions.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2]`, `k = 1`, so every position falls in `slot` 0 and `minPrefix = [0]`.

- `i = 1`: `prefix = 1`, `best = 1 - 0 = 1`; `minPrefix[0]` stays 0.
- `i = 2`: `prefix = 3`, `best = 3 - 0 = 3`; `minPrefix[0]` stays 0.

The answer is 3, the whole array.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(k) for `minPrefix`.

## Pitfalls

- The subarray cannot be empty, so `best` starts at `-Infinity`, not 0: in Example 2 every choice is negative and the answer is -10.
- Use `prefix` before storing it; storing first would compare a position with itself and allow an empty subarray of sum 0.
- Remainders belong to prefix positions 0 to `n`, not to element indexes; forgetting position 0 misses subarrays that start at the front.
- Sums reach 2 · 10^14 in size, so Java and C need 64-bit integers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `minPrefix` | smallest prefix sum seen so far for each remainder class |
| `prefix` | sum of the first `i` elements |
| `slot` | `i % k`, the remainder class of position `i` |
| `best` | largest valid subarray sum found so far |

narration.2: One running minimum of prefix sums for each remainder modulo k; Infinity means none seen yet.
narration.3: Position 0, the empty prefix with sum 0, belongs to remainder class 0.
narration.4: prefix will hold the sum of the first i elements.
narration.5: The answer may be negative, so start below every possible sum.
narration.6: i is a prefix position: how many elements have been added so far.
narration.7: Extend the prefix sum by the next element.
narration.8: Positions with the same remainder are a multiple of k apart.
narration.9: Subtracting the smallest earlier prefix of this class gives the best subarray ending here.
narration.10: Only now record this prefix, so a later position can start a subarray from it.
narration.12: Return the largest sum over all subarrays whose length is a multiple of k.
